title: Artifact decide — arbitrating a spec's or plan's open questions

ground.note: The third draft, drafted and abandoned 2026-10-14, and the base of this one. Its re-grounding stands, and so do its structure, terminology, requirements, surfaces, criteria, question ids and §9 options and losses. This draft changes only what the author's decisions of 2026-10-14 on Q4 and Q15–Q19 require. The Q16 decision went against the third draft's recommendation, so every part written for `frozen-layout` is rewritten for the migrate command.
The third draft's sidecar, with its option ids and its §9 questions Q1–Q4, Q6, Q8–Q12 and Q14–Q19.
The second draft: approved 2026-09-29 at baseline bc84612, abandoned 2026-10-14. It is the origin of the design and of the carried-over answers. Its §11 docs page is kept as it was.
The second draft's sidecar, with the option ids and dates of its §9 answers. Its decided rationales open "Decided by the author on <date>." and its questions carry no suffix marker.

In flight. Eight decided questions, each marked only by a rationale that opens `Decided by the author on 2026-09-2x`, with no suffix on the question. Where the author departed from the recommendation, the rationale says so and `recommendation` names the option chosen.

In flight. Five decided questions, marked the same way, by the rationale only. One reads "against the previous recommendation (`structural`)" with `recommendation: new-oracle-surface`, so the recommendation names the choice.

`spec-approval-record`: `$schema`, then `artifact`, then specFingerprint, approvedAt and a 40-hex baseline. Excess keys are rejected, and no approver is recorded. The old `spec-approvals` ledger shape is kept only to migrate it.
`plan-approval-record`: the same fields plus `sourceSpec` (a path and fingerprint, or null). No approver is recorded. The old `plan-approvals` ledger is read only to migrate it.

One record file per live artifact: `docs/specs/approvals/<spec>.json` and `docs/plans/approvals/<plan>.json`. While an old ledger exists, every command that reads or writes records refuses until `phax artifact migrate-approvals` splits it.

The precedent for a one-time migration. It decides everything before writing and writes nothing on a refusal. It refuses a write-set with uncommitted changes. It writes, then commits exactly those paths in one commit, and prints `nothing to migrate` when there is nothing to do.

Agreement is in-sync, diverged or invalid, computed from the body and the sidecar's rendering with the frontmatter ignored. The remedy for a diverged or invalid sidecar is to re-author the artifact headless, or to delete the sidecar and demote the artifact to hand-authored.

Status and transitions. Approval info is computed for specs only. Approve refuses a diverged or invalid sidecar with exit 12. Reopen (Stale → Draft) clears the `approved` stamp and deletes the plan's record file. A spec's terminal transition is refused while live plans name it. Status and every transition refuse while an old ledger exists.
The transition tables. Specs have no edge back to Draft. A plan reaches Draft only from Stale. Approved → Approved is legal for both kinds.
`fingerprintSource` deletes `status` and `approved` before hashing, so a reopen alone does not change an artifact's fingerprint.
A plan is stale with `spec-changed` evidence when its recorded source-spec fingerprint differs from the spec's current one, and with `self-changed` evidence when its own content differs.

A frozen shape that phax itself never imports; only the schemas package lists it. A frozen module therefore does not by itself mean that phax lifts the format.
Pins the bytes of every frozen module under src/schemas/history/.
A `$schema` stamp names the release that last changed the format's shape. A shape change is a `next` snapshot, which the cut renames to the release. A wording-only schema change moves no stamp.

context:
Headless authoring (0.16.0) made a spec's open questions data. The spec document's `openQuestions[]` use the decision-request shape `{ id, question, options[{ id, label, abandons }], recommendation, rationale }`. phax writes the document as a JSON sidecar (`<stamp>-<slug>.json`) beside the Markdown it renders from it, and the sidecar travels with every lifecycle transition. `artifact approve` refuses with exit 12 when the body is not the sidecar's rendering; the frontmatter never counts. The renderer writes §9 as `## 9. Open questions for implementation planning` and numbers each heading `Q<n>` by position, not by the question's id. Its option bullets and `Recommendation:` line print labels, not option ids.

The data never marks a question as decided. By convention, a question the author has decided stays in `openQuestions`, and its `rationale` opens with `Decided by the author on <date>`. Some specs also append ` (Decided by the author on <date>; not reopened.)` to `question`, as the drafts of this spec do. The two other in-flight specs, `headless-review` and `oracle-phases`, mark their 13 decided questions with the rationale prefix alone. Where the author decided against the recommendation, `recommendation` was rewritten to the option chosen. Nothing in phax reads the marker.

The plan document has no question structure: `preamble.technicalArbitrations` is plain strings. It carries the lineage `sourceSpec` and `completesSpec`, mirrored in the frontmatter as `source-spec` and `completes-spec`. `artifact new plan --spec` requires exactly one of `--last` and `--not-last`. A headless plan seeds the extraction cache with its projection.

The authoring record keeps no provider session id. Since 0.23.0, when the decoder refuses a document, phax retries it by resuming the same session once, within the same process. The id lives only in memory, for that resume and to locate usage, so no authoring session can be resumed after phax exits. `adjust-plan` is the precedent for a session id kept locally (`version: 1`, `sessionId`) and resumed later.

Approvals are recorded in two places:
- an `approved: { date, baseline }` frontmatter stamp;
- one record file per artifact: `docs/specs/approvals/<spec file name>.json` (format `spec-approval-record`: `$schema`, `artifact`, `specFingerprint`, `approvedAt`, `baseline`) or `docs/plans/approvals/<plan file name>.json` (`plan-approval-record`, which adds `sourceSpec`).

Neither records who approved. The old `docs/{specs,plans}/approvals.json` ledgers are read only by `phax artifact migrate-approvals`, and every command that reads or writes approval records refuses while one exists. That command is phax's precedent for a one-time migration. It decides everything before writing, refuses a write-set with uncommitted changes, commits exactly the paths it wrote in one commit, and prints `nothing to migrate` when there is nothing to do. Re-approving an Approved artifact is how an in-place revision is recorded. The fingerprint ignores `status` and `approved`. `artifact status` reports approval for specs only. `phax artifact reopen` moves a Stale plan to Draft: it clears the stamp and deletes the plan's record file. A spec cannot be completed or abandoned while a live plan names it.

Persisted formats are versioned by shape. A file's `$schema` stamp names the release that last changed its format: today spec-document 0.17.0, plan-document 0.20.0, and 0.19.0 for both approval record formats. A shape change is recorded as `packages/schemas/snapshots/<format>/next.schema.json` and released by the cut. The previous shape is frozen under `src/schemas/history/<format>/<release>.ts`, pinned by `packages/schemas/history.lock.json`. Today phax lifts an older file through its frozen shape in one case only: an authoring record manifest stamped 0.17.0 is lifted with `retry: "none"` (0.23.0). Elsewhere it refuses. A plan document stamped 0.17.0–0.19.x lacks `completesSpec` and is refused; its frozen module serves only the schemas package. The rule for provider answers was decided on 2026-10-08: before 1.0, an answer in an older shape of a format that changed is refused by name, never lifted.

The three arbitration doctrines landed at `.claude/skills/phax-decide-spec`, `phax-decide-plan` and `phax-decide-review`, and `package.json` `files` ships them. The skill catalog behind `phax skills install` lists only `phax-planning`, `phax-cli` and `phax-spec`. Each doctrine rests on `E0` (explicit over implicit) and on the pairs `C1`–`C5` with a precedence order. Each adds its own principles, `S1`–`S10`, `P1`–`P9` or `R1`–`R7`, every one a list item that opens with a backticked id. The doctrines describe an interactive mode, a headless mode that decides and escalates, and a later headless-total mode. They output `{ decisions: [{ id, chosen, abandoned[], advocate, why, principles[], reversibility, escalate }] }` and carry no framing questions.

phax runs stay autonomous (decided 2026-10-10). The `decision` class was dropped, `phase-decision-requests` stays parked, and a person reaches a run only through its review notes, after it. Inside a phase worktree, the phase guard refuses every command not classified as allowed, including a new one, and exits 1.

The first consumer is the steme roadmap-1.0 conductor. It authors every spec and plan headless, has their open questions arbitrated, and approves them. When an answer must be reconsidered, it relays a human steering instruction, `rouvre <question>`.
problem:
The open questions are data, but nothing answers them. A loop that wants them decided runs its own arbitration session outside phax: unrecorded, under a private brief, returning prose. The loop then splices that prose into the Markdown by hand, which diverges the sidecar and blocks `approve`.

The answers land nowhere structured. A decision survives only as a prose marker, applied inconsistently across specs, and nothing reads it. Neither `artifact status` nor a later reader can tell which questions are open or decided, on what principle, or what was given up, and approval does not check. A reconsideration such as `rouvre Q3` has no command: `artifact reopen` takes only a Stale plan.

The doctrines exist, but phax neither installs nor loads them, so no citation of `S1` or `P3` can be checked. Finally, an approval issued by a loop is recorded exactly like a human's. An approval record cannot say that no human looked, and an unattended pipeline must never hide that.

productGoal.statement:
phax arbitrates an artifact's open questions with the operator, interactively, as an artifact gesture before any run. A spec or plan carries two sections: open questions and arbitrated questions.

`phax artifact decide` opens a session under the doctrine. The agent first raises the framing questions `F1`–`F5`, then presents the open questions, and the operator decides. The session returns the revised document: each decided question moves to the arbitrated section with its verdict, and the body is revised wherever a verdict departs from the recommendation. phax checks the document deterministically, shows the body diff, and writes only what the operator accepts.

decide runs on Draft only, from a terminal, and never inside a phase worktree. `phax artifact reopen` brings an Approved artifact back to Draft, and `--question` re-arbitrates one question. Approval refuses while the open-questions section is not empty, for headless-authored and hand-authored artifacts alike. Every verdict and every approval names its arbiter.

Each of the four formats this changes gets a new shape. An approval record in an older shape is read through its frozen shape and lifted. Live spec and plan documents are lifted once by `phax artifact migrate-documents`, which re-renders them in the new layout. Until it has run, approve, reopen and decide refuse. No lift presents an old approval or an old decision as an operator's. A headless mode is not specified; it will be built from the decision records these sessions leave.
productGoal.guidingRule: The operator decides. A question is open or arbitrated, never in between, and an arbitration that departs from the recommendation revises the body in the same gesture.

terminology.definition: A question in `openQuestions`, in the decision-request shape { id, question, options[{ id, label, abandons }], recommendation, rationale }.
A question moved to `arbitratedQuestions` with its verdict, keeping every field it had. The earlier verdicts of a re-arbitrated question stay in its `history`.

The answer to one question, in one of two variants. `decided` is the operator's: `chosen` (an option id), `abandoned` (exactly the options not chosen), `why`, `advocate` (the strongest case for an abandoned option), `principles` (cited ids), `reversibility`, `by` (the operator), `at`, and `revised` (the body sections the verdict changed, empty when it changed none). `lifted` is read from a marked question (see Lifted verdict). A plan's decided verdict also carries `phase`.

A question decided before this spec, by convention: its `rationale` opens with `Decided by the author on <YYYY-MM-DD>`. Some marked questions also end their `question` with ` (Decided by the author on <date>; not reopened.)`, but phax does not read that suffix. Where the author decided against the recommendation, `recommendation` was rewritten to the option chosen, so it names the choice.

Reading a file stamped below its format's current shape through the frozen decoder of that shape, then stepping it to the current shape in memory. A lifted approval record stays unchanged on disk until phax next writes it for its own reasons. A lifted spec or plan document is written at its current shape by `phax artifact migrate-documents`.

The verdict a lift gives a marked question. It holds only: `chosen`, the question's recommendation; `abandoned`, its other options; `why`, its rationale; `at`, the marker's date; and `by: { kind: unattributed }`.

`phax artifact migrate-documents`, the one-time command beside `migrate-approvals`. It lifts every live spec and plan sidecar stamped below its document format's current shape, writes the sidecar at that shape and re-renders its body in the new layout, all in one commit.
The body an older sidecar renders to in the layout of the shape it is stamped with. Migration compares a body with it to prove that no hand edit would be overwritten.

`F1`: who consumes this, and what exactly does it read? `F2`: what persists, and how is it read in a year? `F3`: how is a thing identified without its location? `F4`: what can be removed? `F5`: does the cited doctrine still say what the operator intends? phax puts them in the decide prompt, because the doctrine skills do not carry them. The decisive changes of the first real arbitrations (2026-09-28/29) came from these questions, never from the menus.
What an interactive session returns: the artifact's document in its sidecar form, with the decided questions moved to `arbitratedQuestions` and the body revised as their verdicts imply.
`phax artifact decide`, run from a terminal: the framing questions, then the open questions. The operator decides; the agent facilitates and returns the revised document. It is the only mode.
Not specified. It will be built from the decision records that interactive sessions leave: verdicts, departures from the recommendation, and framing corrections.
Who produced a verdict (the operator, or unattributed when lifted), an approval, or an artifact reopen (a machine or the operator).
The cost of undoing a verdict, on the scale cheap | costly | irreversible. It is a cost, not a state: at equal value, the cheaper option is preferred.
The instructions a decide session follows: the doctrine skill for the artifact kind, plus the optional --doctrine file appended after it.
A backticked id that opens a list item in a loaded doctrine, e.g. `S1`, `C4`, `P3`, or a project's `X1`. Verdicts cite principle ids, and phax checks each citation.
The label a caller declares with `--by machine:<grant>` to name the machine performing an approval or an artifact reopen, e.g. roadmap-loop.

A machine approval is recorded with a grant. An operator approval is recorded with the committing git identity. An unattributed approval has no recorded approver; every record written before this change is lifted to it.
The record phax writes on phax/records/v1 for one decide session.

`phax artifact reopen <path>`: today, it moves a Stale plan back to Draft. This spec extends it to move an Approved spec or plan back to Draft. It is the only way to arbitrate an approved artifact again.
An approval or an artifact reopen given with `--by operator`, or without `--by` from a terminal. The operator is named by the committing git identity.

The layout the renderer gives both sections. A hand-authored artifact follows it so that phax can read it. A spec has a `## 9. Open questions` section and a `## 9b. Arbitrated questions` section. Each question is a `### <id> — <question>` heading, followed by one bullet per option, `- <option id> — <label> — abandons: <loss>`, and a `Recommendation: <option id> — <rationale>` line. In the arbitrated section, the `Decision:` block follows. A plan puts both sections in its preamble, as `## Open questions` and `## Arbitrated questions`.

requirements.title: An interactive session
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax artifact decide` runs THE system SHALL open an interactive session in which the agent first raises the framing questions `F1`–`F5` and then presents the open questions; the operator decides, and the agent returns the revised document. The session SHALL resume the artifact's authoring session when its id is kept, start a new one otherwise, and print which it did.

requirements.title: Authoring session id kept locally
requirements.statement: WHEN a headless authoring session is spawned THE system SHALL keep its provider session id in local state outside the records branch, and, when the session is retried, the id of the retried session.

requirements.title: Model and effort
requirements.statement: The system SHALL resolve the decide session's model and effort from `--model` and `--effort` when they are given, and from the built-in catalog default otherwise.

requirements.title: Questions come from the sidecar
requirements.statement: WHEN `decide` reads an artifact that has an in-sync sidecar at its format's current shape THE system SHALL take the questions from the sidecar's `openQuestions` and `arbitratedQuestions`.

requirements.title: Questions from a hand-authored §9
requirements.statement: WHEN `decide` reads an artifact that has no sidecar THE system SHALL take its open and arbitrated questions from its two sections in the §9 format, and SHALL refuse before any session, naming the first line that departs from the format, if they do not parse.

requirements.title: Hand-authored decisions written in place
requirements.statement: WHEN verdicts land on a hand-authored artifact THE system SHALL move each decided question's block from the open-questions section to the arbitrated-questions section with its `Decision:` block, apply the body edits the operator accepted, and append the entries to the decision log, changing no other line.

requirements.title: Artifact preconditions
requirements.statement: IF the artifact is not Draft, its sidecar is diverged or invalid, or the artifact or its sidecar has uncommitted changes THEN the system SHALL refuse `decide` with exit 12 before any session; for an Approved or Stale artifact, the refusal SHALL name `phax artifact reopen <path>`.

requirements.title: Interactive only
requirements.statement: IF `phax artifact decide` runs without a terminal THEN the system SHALL refuse with exit 12 before any session, stating that decide is interactive only.

requirements.title: Never inside a run
requirements.statement: IF `phax artifact decide` runs inside a phase worktree THEN the system SHALL refuse it with the phase guard's refusal and exit 1 before any session.

requirements.title: Presentation order
requirements.statement: WHEN `decide` starts THE system SHALL present, in order: the framing questions `F1`–`F5`; then the question named by `--question`, with its verdict when it is arbitrated; then the open questions.

requirements.title: Nothing to decide
requirements.statement: IF the open-questions section is empty and `--question` is not given THEN the system SHALL spawn no session, write nothing, and exit 0, stating that there is nothing to decide.

requirements.title: Doctrine skill by artifact kind
requirements.statement: The system SHALL load the doctrine skill `phax-decide-spec` into a decide session on a spec, and `phax-decide-plan` into a decide session on a plan.

requirements.title: Project skill replaces the default
requirements.statement: WHERE a skill of the same name is installed at project scope for the session's provider THE system SHALL load it in place of the bundled doctrine skill.

requirements.title: Doctrine file appended
requirements.statement: WHERE `--doctrine <file>` is given THE system SHALL append the file's content after the doctrine skill in the session prompt.

requirements.title: Principle ids collected
requirements.statement: The system SHALL take as the citable principle ids the backticked ids that open list items in the loaded doctrine skill and in the `--doctrine` file.

requirements.title: Doctrine file refused
requirements.statement: IF the `--doctrine` file cannot be read, defines no principle id, or defines a principle id that the loaded skill also defines THEN the system SHALL refuse with exit 12 before spawning.

requirements.title: Only a revised document lands
requirements.statement: WHEN a decide session ends THE system SHALL land only a revised document that validates against the artifact kind's document schema at its current shape.

requirements.title: The answer names its shape
requirements.statement: IF the revised document carries no `$schema`, or a `$schema` that names another format or a shape other than the artifact kind's current one THEN the system SHALL refuse it with exit 5, naming the `$schema` URL it reads, and SHALL never lift it.

requirements.title: Invalid decisions land nothing
requirements.statement: IF the session returns no document, returns something that is not JSON or fails the schema, or returns a document with any of the violations below THEN the system SHALL fail with exit 5, naming the first violation by path, and SHALL leave the working tree and HEAD unchanged. The violations: it moves a question that was not presented; it changes an open question it did not decide, or an arbitrated question other than the one being re-arbitrated; it chooses an option the question does not list; it lists as abandoned anything other than exactly the unchosen options; it cites a principle id that no loaded doctrine defines; it breaks traceability (an acceptance criterion without its requirement, or a requirement left uncovered); or, on a plan, it names a phase the plan does not have.

requirements.title: A decided question moves with its verdict
requirements.statement: WHEN the operator decides a question THE system SHALL move it from `openQuestions` to `arbitratedQuestions` with a `decided` verdict, keeping every field it had.

requirements.title: A verdict revises the body it implies
requirements.statement: WHEN a verdict departs from its question's recommendation THE revised document SHALL carry the body changes the verdict implies (requirements, surface, acceptance criteria, planning note), and the verdict SHALL name the sections it revised in `revised`.

requirements.title: The operator accepts the body diff
requirements.statement: WHEN an interactive session returns its revised document THE system SHALL show the operator the diff of the rendered body before writing anything, and SHALL write nothing unless the operator accepts it.

requirements.title: Rate and usage limits
requirements.statement: IF a decide session ends on a provider rate or usage limit THEN the system SHALL fail in the existing rate-limit exit family with nothing written.

requirements.title: Artifact changed during the session
requirements.statement: IF the artifact or its sidecar changed while the decide session ran THEN the system SHALL refuse with exit 12 to write the decisions back, leaving those changes in place and committing nothing.

requirements.title: Decision attribution
requirements.statement: The system SHALL attribute each `decided` verdict to the operator, named by the committing git identity, and SHALL record the loaded doctrine sources and the session's provider, model and effort.

requirements.title: Artifact re-rendered
requirements.statement: WHEN a decide document lands THE system SHALL write the sidecar at its format's current shape and re-render the artifact with its deterministic renderer: the open questions, then the arbitrated questions with their verdicts (decided or lifted), then a decision log listing every verdict in order.

requirements.title: Questions are named by id
requirements.statement: The system SHALL head every rendered question with its id, open every option bullet and the `Recommendation:` line with an option id, and name questions by id in `--question`, `artifact status`, refusals and the decision log.

requirements.title: One commit
requirements.statement: WHEN `decide` writes an artifact THE system SHALL commit exactly the paths it wrote in one commit: the artifact and its sidecar, or the hand-authored artifact alone.

requirements.title: Commit failure
requirements.statement: IF the commit made by `decide` or by `migrate-documents` fails THEN the system SHALL report an artifact error with exit 12 and leave the files written but uncommitted.

requirements.title: Decision record
requirements.statement: WHEN a decide session ends after spawning and records are enabled THE system SHALL write a decision record whose manifest is stamped with its format's shape. The record SHALL carry: the prompt; the doctrine sources with their fingerprints; the questions presented; the landed document and the body diff the operator accepted; the count of questions arbitrated and the count of verdicts that departed from the recommendation; the transcript (per the records transcript setting); provider, model, effort and usage; the outcome, committed or failed; and the commit when there is one.

requirements.title: Re-rendered plan never re-extracted
requirements.statement: WHEN `decide` or `migrate-documents` re-renders or rewrites a plan THE system SHALL re-seed the extraction cache with the plan's projection, so that `phax run` never extracts it through a model.

requirements.title: A re-rendered plan keeps its lineage
requirements.statement: WHEN `decide` or `migrate-documents` re-renders a plan THE system SHALL keep its `sourceSpec` and `completesSpec`, and its frontmatter `source-spec` and `completes-spec`, exactly as they were.

requirements.title: Re-arbitrating one question
requirements.statement: WHERE `--question <id>` names an arbitrated question THE system SHALL present it with its verdict and, on a new verdict, keep the previous one in its history; WHERE it names an open question THE session SHALL take that question alone.

requirements.title: Unknown question refused
requirements.statement: IF `--question` names a question the artifact does not have THEN the system SHALL refuse with exit 12 before any session, naming the artifact's question ids, and write nothing.

requirements.title: Artifact reopen from Approved
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax artifact reopen` is given an Approved spec or plan THE system SHALL move it to Draft, clear its `approved` stamp, delete its approval record file, and commit the write-set in one commit whose trailer names the gesture's arbiter. Stale → Draft for plans is unchanged, apart from naming the arbiter.

requirements.title: Artifact reopen refusals
requirements.statement: IF `phax artifact reopen` is given a Draft, Completed or Abandoned artifact THEN the system SHALL refuse with exit 12 and write nothing.

requirements.title: Reopening a spec leaves its plans
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax artifact reopen` moves an Approved spec to Draft THE system SHALL leave every live plan bound to it unchanged and name each one in its output.

requirements.title: Approval requires no open question
requirements.statement: IF the open-questions section of a spec or plan is not empty, in its sidecar or, when hand-authored, in the §9 format THEN `phax artifact approve` SHALL refuse with exit 12, naming the open questions and `phax artifact decide <path>`.

requirements.title: A hand-authored §9 must parse
requirements.statement: IF a hand-authored artifact has question sections that do not parse in the §9 format THEN `phax artifact approve` SHALL refuse with exit 12, naming the first line that departs. An artifact with neither section is approved with no question check.

requirements.title: Machine gestures
requirements.statement: WHERE `--by machine:<grant>` is given to `phax artifact approve` or `phax artifact reopen` THE system SHALL record that gesture as performed by a machine, naming the grant.

requirements.title: Operator gestures
requirements.statement: WHEN `--by operator` is given, or no `--by` is given and the command runs from a terminal, THE system SHALL record the approval or reopen as performed by the operator, named by the committing git identity.

requirements.title: No terminal, no default
requirements.statement: IF `phax artifact approve` or `phax artifact reopen` runs without `--by` and not from a terminal THEN the system SHALL refuse with exit 12, naming `--by operator` and `--by machine:<grant>`.

requirements.title: New approvals name their approver
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax artifact approve` writes an approval record file THE system SHALL write it at its format's new shape, with an `approvedBy` that names the machine's grant or the operator.

requirements.title: Older approval records are lifted, never refused
requirements.statement: WHEN phax reads an approval record file stamped 0.19.0, or splits an old approvals ledger, THE system SHALL lift each record through its frozen shape to `approvedBy: { kind: unattributed }`, and SHALL leave a record file that it only reads unchanged on disk.

requirements.title: Unattributed approvals stay unattributed
requirements.statement: WHEN phax reads an approval recorded or lifted as unattributed THE system SHALL present it as unattributed, never as an operator approval.

requirements.title: Older spec documents are lifted by the rationale marker
requirements.statement: WHEN phax lifts a spec document stamped below its format's current shape THE system SHALL move to `arbitratedQuestions`, with a lifted verdict and an empty history, each question whose `rationale` opens with `Decided by the author on <YYYY-MM-DD>`, and SHALL leave every other question open, whatever its `question` text says.

requirements.title: A lifted verdict invents nothing
requirements.statement: WHEN phax lifts a marked question THE system SHALL give it a `lifted` verdict that holds only its recommendation as `chosen`, its other options as `abandoned`, its rationale as `why`, the marker's date as `at`, and `by: { kind: unattributed }`; it SHALL present the verdict as lifted and unattributed, never as an operator's.

requirements.title: Older plan documents are lifted
requirements.statement: WHEN phax reads a plan document stamped 0.20.0 THE system SHALL lift it with empty `openQuestions` and `arbitratedQuestions` in its preamble; a plan document stamped 0.17.0–0.19.x stays refused, as it is today.

requirements.title: Document migration
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax artifact migrate-documents` runs THE system SHALL lift every live spec and plan sidecar stamped below its document format's current shape, write it at that shape, and re-render its body in the new layout, keeping its frontmatter as it was.

requirements.title: Migration never overwrites a hand edit
requirements.statement: IF a live sidecar to migrate is invalid, its body is not the sidecar's own-shape rendering, or a path the command would write has uncommitted changes THEN `phax artifact migrate-documents` SHALL refuse with exit 12 before writing anything, naming each such artifact and its remedy.

requirements.title: Migration names what it unsettles
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax artifact migrate-documents` migrates THE system SHALL report each migrated artifact with its status and question counts. It SHALL also name each Approved artifact that now reads edited since approval, with its open questions when it has any, and each live plan that the migration leaves stale with `spec-changed` evidence.

requirements.title: Migration in one commit
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax artifact migrate-documents` writes THE system SHALL commit exactly the paths it rewrote in one commit.

requirements.title: Nothing to migrate
requirements.statement: IF no live spec or plan sidecar is stamped below its document format's current shape THEN `phax artifact migrate-documents` SHALL write nothing, make no commit, and exit 0, stating that there is nothing to migrate.

requirements.title: Approval waits for migration
requirements.statement: IF any live spec or plan sidecar is stamped below its document format's current shape THEN `phax artifact approve`, `phax artifact reopen` and `phax artifact decide` SHALL refuse with exit 12 before writing anything, naming the sidecar and `phax artifact migrate-documents`.

requirements.title: Status names an unmigrated sidecar
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax artifact status` inspects an artifact whose sidecar is stamped below its document format's current shape THE system SHALL report the sidecar's stamped shape and `phax artifact migrate-documents` in place of an agreement value, and report its questions as lifted.

requirements.title: Status reports questions
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax artifact status` inspects an artifact that has question sections THE system SHALL report the number of open and arbitrated questions, how many of the arbitrated ones are lifted, the ids of the open ones, and the decide command that answers them.

requirements.title: Status names the approver
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax artifact status` reports an approval of a spec or a plan THE system SHALL name the approver's kind and identity: machine and grant, operator and name, or unattributed.

requirements.title: Doctrine skills ship and install
requirements.statement: The system SHALL list `phax-decide-spec`, `phax-decide-plan` and `phax-decide-review` in its bundled skill catalog, so that `phax skills install` installs them exactly as it installs `phax-spec`.

requirements.title: Plan open questions
requirements.statement: WHERE the artifact is a plan THE system SHALL read its questions from the plan document's `openQuestions` and `arbitratedQuestions` in the preamble, in the same shapes as a spec's.

requirements.title: Authoring emits open questions only
requirements.statement: IF the document returned by an authoring session carries an arbitrated question THEN the system SHALL reject it as an invalid document.

nonGoals: Headless arbitration. It will be built from the decision records that interactive sessions leave (verdicts, departures from the recommendation, framing corrections). There is no machine proposal, no escalation and no machine reversal.
A decision queue UI or desktop inbox. This spec provides the data and the status line, nothing visual.
Multi-human arbitration: several operators, votes, required reviewers or per-question owners. The operator is whoever commits.

Arbitration during a run. decide is an artifact gesture before any run, and it is refused inside a phase worktree. Answering run decision requests (`phase-decision-requests` stays parked), any mid-run stop for a person, and autopilot loops are out of scope.
Editing a question's wording or its options from within decide. The body is revised only as a verdict implies, and only once the operator accepts the diff.
Writing the doctrine skills' text. It is the author's, and their headless sections stay unused until a headless mode is specified.
`headless-review`, which reopens after this spec ships and adopts its approver form, and loading `phax-decide-review` from decide. That skill ships here, and review-plan consumes it.
`oracle-phases`, which needs re-authoring on its own.
Changing how headless authoring loads `phax-spec` and `phax-planning`. The project-skill override applies to the decide doctrines only.
A `phax.json` key for the decide model and effort. One can be added later without breaking anything.
Parsing a steering file. Mapping `rouvre Q3` to `phax artifact reopen` plus `decide --question Q3` is the caller's job.
The approver in the frontmatter `approved` stamp. The approval record file is the single source of who approved.

A migration command for approval records. A 0.19.0 record is lifted on read and rewritten at the new shape only when the next approval writes it (§9 Q4); `migrate-documents` migrates spec and plan documents only.
Migrating archived (Completed or Abandoned) artifacts, or hand-authored ones. `migrate-documents` touches live sidecars only; a hand-authored §9 is converted to the §9 format once, by hand.

Re-approving the artifacts that migration leaves edited since approval, or refreshing the plans it leaves stale. The command names them; the operator re-approves them, or reopens and decides them first.
Blocking `phax artifact complete` and `phax artifact abandon` until migration. They carry an older sidecar as it is, as they carry any sidecar today.
Reading plan documents stamped 0.17.0–0.19.x, which stay refused as today.
Extracting open questions from a free-form Markdown layout.
Changing the authoring answer's `version: 1` form, or promising stability for these formats beyond the provider-answer rule decided on 2026-10-08.

options.label: The caller declares it with `--machine <grant>`. Without the flag, the gesture is the operator's.
options.abandons: enforcement: a loop that omits the flag is recorded as the operator, so attribution is honest by declaration only

options.abandons: determinism and scripted operators: the same command records differently depending on the terminal, and a human's scripted approval is labelled machine

options.abandons: every existing `artifact approve` invocation: a breaking CLI change against the additive constraint

options.label: `--by operator | machine:<grant>`, required when not run from a terminal; from a terminal without it, the operator.
options.abandons: an unchanged scripted `approve`: every non-terminal caller must add `--by`

options.abandons: attribution written in the file itself: an untouched 0.19.0 record says nothing on disk, and every reader (phax, the schemas package) must apply the same lift to read it as unattributed

arbitratedQuestions.rationale: Decided by the author on 2026-10-14, as recommended. The 2026-09-28 answer chose refusal when approvals were a shared ledger whose shape had no name. The loss is bounded: a lifted record is rewritten at the next approval, and deleted by reopen, completion or abandonment.

settled: One mode, interactive: the framing questions `F1`–`F5`, the operator's verdicts, the revised document, and the body diff accepted before writing (Q14). There is no `--headless`, no machine proposal, no escalation and no machine reversal. decide refuses without a terminal and, through the phase guard, inside a phase worktree: it never runs inside a run.
Two sections, `openQuestions` and `arbitratedQuestions`. A decided question moves with its verdict, and approval requires the open section to be empty (Q11, Q9).

A verdict that departs from the recommendation revises the body in the same document. phax checks what moved, what stayed and traceability, shows the body diff, and writes only what the operator accepts (Q12).
The three doctrine skills are registered in the skill catalog and install like `phax-spec`.

Doctrine resolution: `phax-decide-spec` or `phax-decide-plan` by kind, a project-scope copy of the same name winning over the bundled one, and `--doctrine` appended after it. Principle ids are the backticked ids that open list items, and every citation is validated; this format is decided, not open. decide's prompt carries the framing questions, because the doctrine skills do not hold them.
The input is the sidecar at its current shape or, for a hand-authored artifact, its §9 in the §9 format (Q6, Q10). With nothing awaiting decision, decide exits 0 with no session.

decide runs on Draft only. `phax artifact reopen` extends to Approved → Draft, clearing the stamp and deleting the approval record file (Q1); it leaves bound plans as they are and names them (Q18). `--question` re-arbitrates one question, and there is no reopened state (Q8).

Approver attribution in both approval record formats: `--by machine:<grant>`, `--by operator`, the operator by default from a terminal, and a refusal without a terminal (Q3). A 0.19.0 record is lifted on read to unattributed (Q4). Plans gain structured `openQuestions` and `arbitratedQuestions` (Q2).

Formats: `spec-document`, `plan-document`, `spec-approval-record` and `plan-approval-record` get new shapes, and a decision record manifest is born with `$schema`. Each older file is read as §6's format table states. The decide session answers in the sidecar form at the current shape, and any other stamp is refused by name (Q19).

Spec documents lift by the rationale marker alone; the question suffix is not read (Q15). Questions are named by id in the Markdown, on the command line, in status, refusals and the decision log (Q17).

Document migration (Q16): `phax artifact migrate-documents` lifts every live spec and plan sidecar stamped below its document shape and re-renders its body, once. It refuses, writing nothing, on an invalid sidecar, a body that is not its sidecar's own-shape rendering, or uncommitted changes on a path it would write. It names every Approved artifact left edited since approval and every plan left stale, and commits exactly the paths it rewrote. Until it has run, approve, reopen and decide refuse, naming it; complete and abandon carry an older sidecar as it is.

Left to the plan, as §6 marks indicative: the rendering prose of the Decision block and decision-log entries, and the plan preamble section names; the spelling of the `--by` values, the reopen trailer, `history`, `verdict`, `approvedBy` and their nested keys, and the decision record's format id and manifest layout; how the session hands its revised document to phax and how the diff is shown and accepted; whether the session returns a decided verdict's `by` and `at` for phax to check, or phax sets them; where the authoring session id is kept in local state; how a provider whose skills live in `.agents/skills` resolves the project override (following `phax skills install`'s target mapping); the built-in decide model and effort, chosen from the catalog on cost; and `migrate-documents`' output layout and commit subject.
constraints: Compose the headless-authoring machinery: prompt assembly, the JSON-only provider session, boundary decoding, deterministic renderers, the path-scoped commit, the record writer and the sidecar agreement check. Do not fork it.

For a headless-authored artifact, the sidecar's `openQuestions` and `arbitratedQuestions` are the single source of a question's state. For a hand-authored one, its two §9 sections are, parsed deterministically. §9, the decision log, `artifact status` and the approve refusal all derive from that source.

New persisted fields are required and use explicit per-variant enums: `arbitratedQuestions` in both documents, `openQuestions` in the plan preamble, `verdict` and `history` on every arbitrated question, and `approvedBy` on every approval record at the new shape. `approvedBy.kind` is machine | operator | unattributed, and `verdict.kind` is decided | lifted. No field becomes optional. The authoring answer gains `arbitratedQuestions`, which must be empty.

Each changed format records its new shape as `packages/schemas/snapshots/<format>/next.schema.json`, released by the cut (`docs/release.md`). Its previous shape is frozen under `src/schemas/history/<format>/<release>.ts` and pinned by `packages/schemas/history.lock.json`, and phax's reader lifts through it as it lifts the authoring record manifest. A frozen-shape lift is the sanctioned way to read an older file; it is not a back-compat shim.

Agreement compares a body with its sidecar's rendering at the current shape only; no older §9 layout is kept for it. The one use of an older shape's rendering is `migrate-documents`' check that a body is untouched before the command re-renders it. Plan question sections render only when non-empty.

`migrate-documents` follows `migrate-approvals`: it decides everything before writing anything, refuses a dirty write-set, writes, then commits exactly the paths it rewrote in one commit, and keeps frontmatter, `approved` stamps and approval record files as they are.

A re-rendered plan, whether by decide or by migration, must still pass `phax plans lint`, parse on the deterministic path to the same projection, have its extraction cache re-seeded, and keep its lineage.
The local authoring session id never goes to the records branch, so the authoring record format is unchanged.

Transitions keep carrying the sidecar in their write-set, and the clean-file precondition of artifact auto-commits applies to decide, artifact reopen and migrate-documents. Approval commands keep refusing while an old approvals ledger exists; approve, reopen and decide also refuse while a live sidecar is stamped below its document shape.
`artifact decide` and `artifact migrate-documents` are classified `refused` in the phase guard's classification.

The CLI stays additive: two new commands, new flags and new transitions. The only non-additive behaviors are Q3's decided refusal of `approve` and `reopen` without `--by` outside a terminal, and Q16's one-time refusal of approve, reopen and decide until `migrate-documents` has run.
The machine/operator approval form is shared with the headless-review spec, which reopens after this spec ships and adopts it.
A project that installs the default skills at project scope pins that copy. The decision record's skill source and fingerprint make that drift visible; nothing else is added for it.

The landed doctrine skills describe a headless mode that decides and escalates. decide loads them for the interactive session, whose facilitation they guide, and their headless sections stay unused until a headless mode is specified.
Every example and test fixture is made up; none is copied from another repository.

docsPage.reader: An operator who wants a spec's or plan's open questions decided under a written doctrine: framing first, then each question, seeing what each verdict changed in the body, and telling a machine's approval from a human's.

phax artifact new spec plan-prune --headless --brief brief.md
phax artifact status docs/specs/2609251400-plan-prune.md
  Questions: 3 — open 3 (Q1, Q2, Q3) · arbitrated 0
phax artifact decide docs/specs/2609251400-plan-prune.md          # framing F1–F5, then decide; accept the body diff
phax artifact approve docs/specs/2609251400-plan-prune.md --by operator
phax artifact reopen docs/specs/2609251400-plan-prune.md --by operator     # back to Draft to reconsider
phax artifact decide docs/specs/2609251400-plan-prune.md --question Q1     # re-arbitrate one question; the old verdict stays in its history
